solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Untimely errors made by chairman's son

indicators.note: made here means fashioned or constructed afresh, so the letters that follow are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and its S is kept as a letter of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company boss's son has made some badly timed blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all of CHAIRMANS plus SON, twelve letters, with 'made' as the signal to rearrange them.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed in the wrong period of time are chronological mistakes, hence untimely errors.

clue.text: Apprehensive over bursting into sunset

indicators.note: into places the burst letters inside the other piece
set means arranged or put in order, a signal to rearrange the letters of sun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bursting suggests the word over breaking apart so its letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about something breaking out across a sunset sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'sunset' as evening, but the setter splits that one word in two, so its second half is the anagram signal for its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apprehensive is uneasy and fearful, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drink to the end of the rooster?

parts.note: a rooster is a male chicken, a cock
the tail is the hind end of a bird

explanation.surface: A whimsical toast raised to the farmyard bird's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'end of the rooster', the rooster's end is its tail, giving COCK then TAIL in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed alcoholic beverage of spirits and other ingredients is a classic example of a drink.

clue.text: Luxurious hotel provides legal documents at a hearing

indicators.note: a hearing is a court session but here means heard spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: writs are formal written court orders

explanation.surface: A grand hotel supplies the paperwork for a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a hearing' fakes a legal context to match 'legal documents'. The Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London's Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: The London establishment of that name is a byword for opulent accommodation, an example of a luxurious hotel.

clue.text: Pink gin ran out, put to use at the table

definitions.text: put to use at the table

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, signalling the letters of those three words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The bar ran dry of pink gin, so the drinkers had to make do at their table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran out' reads as a single phrase meaning exhausted, but only 'out' is the signal; 'ran' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular holder for a folded serviette is an item used when dining at the table.

clue.text: Just one line from a letter

definitions.text: Just one line from a letter

parts.words: Just one line from a letter
parts.note: suggests a single sentence quoted from correspondence, but means a small stroke projecting from a printed character

explanation.surface: Someone quotes only one line from a letter they received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' means a typed character, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography the small finishing stroke at the end of a character's main strokes is a single short line on that character.

clue.text: Moved by a little spooning?

parts.note: suggests being emotionally touched by some kissing and cuddling, but means being mixed with a spoon

explanation.surface: Someone touched by a little romantic cuddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooning' is old slang for courting, but here it is literal use of a spoon; 'moved' covers both feelings and mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea or soup agitated with a spoon has been mixed round, while a person deeply touched is emotionally affected too.

clue.text: Circulated counterfeit US money, but shifted responsibility

definitions.meaning: literally, handed on a forged dollar, since a buck is US slang for a dollar
the idiom for handing a duty or blame on to someone else

explanation.surface: A con artist spreads fake dollars and blames somebody else when caught.
explanation.walkthrough: A buck is informal American for a dollar; the idiom comes from a marker in poker passed to the next dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means evading blame by pushing the duty elsewhere; literally it describes handing on a dollar bill.

clue.text: Could be a circular plug

definitions.meaning: a printed notice sent round to many people to promote something
informal for a piece of publicity promoting a product

explanation.surface: Something round that might be a stopper in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'circular' and 'plug' pretend to describe a round bung; each is a kind of publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotional leaflet sent round and a quick piece of publicity are both forms of commercial promotion.

clue.text: Almost a full month before bed bears fruit

indicators.note: before places the shortened month ahead of the next piece
almost means not quite complete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: April is a full calendar month
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A month of growth before bedtime leaves the tree heavy with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts APRIL to APRI.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-yellow stone fruit is a kind of fruit related to the plum and peach.

clue.text: Warded off quiet raider in disguise

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance changed, so the letters of raider are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fends off a silent intruder who is wearing a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges RAIDER into ARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect a blow or an awkward question is to ward it off; a fencing term in origin.

clue.text: A good man dismissed for drink

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is the crossword's stock good man
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A decent fellow is turned away in favour of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' is the cricket sense: a batter who is dismissed is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dark beer brewed with roasted malt, such as porter's heavier cousin, is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Hymn for church service?

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody, as a hymn is
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A request for a hymn suitable for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service but is an armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: The aerial branch of the military is one of the armed services.

clue.text: Exultant about Mini repair being cancelled

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the joyful word goes round the other piece

parts.note: exultant and elated both mean overjoyed

indicators.note: repair means fixing, so the letters of the car's name are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about a Mini being fixed, but the job is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mini' looks like the car, a classic small British model, but is just four letters for 'repair' to reorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something knocked out or removed has been eliminated, so cancelled and wiped out are synonyms.

clue.text: It raises the spirit

parts.note: suggests something cheering, but means a place producing alcoholic spirits

explanation.surface: Something that lifts one's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' is whisky or gin, not morale; 'raises' means produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where whisky or gin is made produces spirits, so it literally brings the spirit into being.

clue.text: It needs a key first for opening

indicators.note: first places the article and key ahead of the pronoun

parts.note: D is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something can only be unlocked with a key used first.
explanation.walkthrough: An adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: This mining term is a horizontal passage into a hillside, an entrance or opening to the workings.

clue.text: Seems upset about flag signals

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shuffled letters surround the other piece
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of seems are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
to flag is to droop or tire, to sag

explanation.surface: Someone appears unsettled by the business of flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges SEEMS to MESES, which goes about SAG; 'flag' is the verb meaning to wilt, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Communications passed on are signals, as with flag semaphore; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Vagrant who needs nothing more than a warm place

parts.note: a hob is the hot top of a cooker or a shelf by the fire
O is the zero digit, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A homeless person wants nothing beyond somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than' reads as a comparison but here sets the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A wandering homeless person, originally an American migrant worker, is a tramp or vagrant.

clue.text: A factor in debt-collection

parts.note: suggests one element of the process, but a factor is also an agent, and this officer collects debts

explanation.surface: One consideration in the business of recovering money owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'factor' means an agent or steward, chiefly in Scotland, not an element.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer who seizes goods for unpaid debts is an agent in collecting them; such an officer is also an estate manager.

clue.text: Secretary uses name Susan, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, a signal to rework the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A secretary goes by the fancy name Susan, or so I imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uses' is only a link; the fodder is NAME, SUSAN and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to write from dictation or copy manuscripts is a literary assistant, a secretary.

clue.text: Sign that has a sting in its tail

definitions.text: Sign that has a sting in its tail

parts.words: Sign that has a sting in its tail
parts.note: the idiom means an unpleasant surprise at the end, but this zodiac sign is the ..., stinger in the tail

explanation.surface: A notice with a nasty surprise at its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' is a zodiac sign whose emblem, the scorpion, literally has a sting in its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth sign of the zodiac is represented by a scorpion, whose venomous sting is at the tip of its tail.

clue.text: Instruction for barristers and aircrew

parts.note: barristers receive briefs from solicitors, and pilots get pre-flight instructions; one word covers both

explanation.surface: Guidance given both to lawyers in court and to flight crews.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a barrister is a courtroom lawyer who is engaged by a solicitor's brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving instructions or information before a task, whether to a barrister or a flight crew, is the same process.

clue.text: He takes to his bed — sharpish

definitions.text: He takes to his bed — sharpish

parts.words: He takes to his bed — sharpish
parts.note: suggests someone going to bed quickly, but alludes to the ascetic who lies on a bed of nails

explanation.surface: A man heading off to bed in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharpish' means quickly, but here hints at the sharp nails of the holy man's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu or Muslim ascetic wonder-worker is traditionally pictured lying on a bed of sharp nails.

clue.text: Natural outburst

parts.note: suggests a spontaneous emotional outburst, but means a violent upheaval of nature, a tempest

explanation.surface: An outburst that comes quite naturally to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' means of the natural world, not spontaneous.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest of wind and rain is a violent disturbance of the weather, an outburst of nature; it can also be an emotional outburst.

clue.text: State obstruction to an alliance

indicators.note: state as a verb means say aloud, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a block is something that obstructs

explanation.surface: A country putting up a barrier against an alliance of nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, fitting the alliance, but is the verb 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nations or parties acting together, like the old Eastern one, is an alliance.

clue.text: Just an insect — but a game one

definitions.meaning: a chirping insect related to the grasshopper
the bat-and-ball sport played on a pitch with wickets

explanation.surface: Something dismissed as a mere insect turns out to be a plucky one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' in the surface means plucky; here it is a sport, the English bat-and-ball game with wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a chirping grasshopper-like insect and the English summer sport played with bat and ball.

clue.text: Member starting to pirouette makes the ball change direction

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
a pirouette is a spin on one foot

explanation.surface: A dancer's limb begins a twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket this style of bowling turns the ball off the pitch from leg side to off side.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket bowling technique imparts rotation so the ball deviates after bouncing, changing its line.

clue.text: Settlement by a company shows stout resolution

indicators.note: by means next to, so the company goes beside the settlement word

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a settlement of a question is a decision on it

explanation.surface: A company's agreement to settle shows real determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts FIRM beside DECISION, ahead of it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A resolve that is resolute and unwavering is a strong, settled determination.
